title: KYC and Onboarding Document Verification for Brokers
summary: Check account opening packets for brokers and depository participants: cross-match KYC fields, apply segment and entity checklists, and prepare a discrepancy list for the checker.

seo.title: Broker KYC and Onboarding Verification AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI for brokers and DPs that cross-checks PAN, masked Aadhaar, address, bank and income proofs, applies KYC checklists and prepares files for checkers.

problem.intro: Every trading and demat account starts with a KYC packet: PAN, masked Aadhaar or DigiLocker e-KYC, address and bank proof, signature, in-person verification and nomination details, plus income proof if the client wants derivatives. Checkers verify each packet before upload to a KRA, and volumes surge whenever a popular IPO opens.

pain_points.title: Name and address mismatches
pain_points.detail: Small differences between PAN, Aadhaar, bank records and the application lead to KRA rejections that send the client back to the start.

pain_points.title: Derivatives activation needs judgement
pain_points.detail: Income proofs range from ITRs and salary slips to bank statements and holding statements, and checkers must confirm each meets your policy.

pain_points.title: Non-individual and NRI files are slow
pain_points.detail: Company, partnership, trust, HUF and NRI accounts each need different documents, and missing items surface late.

pain_points.title: Checker queues spike unpredictably
pain_points.detail: IPO openings and market rallies bring sudden volume, and quality slips when checkers rush.

solution.overview: We build a maker-checker assistant for your onboarding team. It classifies every document in the packet, extracts names, dates of birth, PAN, addresses, bank details and signatures, and cross-matches them with each other and with the record fetched from the KRA or CKYC. It applies checklists for the client's entity type and requested segments, checks that derivatives requests carry an acceptable income proof, and confirms expiry dates and legibility. Mismatches and missing items become a discrepancy list with document references and a drafted message for the client. Clean files go to a checker for fast approval; no account is approved without a person.
capabilities: Classifies PAN, masked Aadhaar or DigiLocker e-KYC, address proofs, bank proofs, income proofs and entity documents
Cross-matches name, date of birth, address and PAN across documents and the KRA or CKYC record
Applies checklists by entity type: individual, NRI, HUF, partnership, company or trust
Checks that derivatives segment requests carry an acceptable income proof under your policy
Verifies presence of signature, photograph, nomination or opt-out declaration and FATCA self-certification
Produces a discrepancy list and a drafted client message, with a maker-checker audit trail

workflow.title: Receive the packet
workflow.detail: The application and documents arrive from your e-KYC journey, branch or partner channel.

workflow.title: Classify and extract
workflow.detail: Each document is identified and key fields are extracted, with Aadhaar masked on capture.

workflow.title: Cross-match records
workflow.detail: Fields are compared across documents and with the KRA or CKYC record.

workflow.title: Apply checklists
workflow.detail: Entity-type and segment checklists confirm the required documents and an acceptable income proof.

workflow.title: Checker review
workflow.detail: Files with discrepancies go to a checker with a drafted client message; clean files go to a checker for fast approval.

workflow.title: Upload and record
workflow.detail: Approved records are uploaded to the KRA and back office, and the audit trail is stored.

inputs: Account opening form and application data
PAN, masked Aadhaar or DigiLocker e-KYC, and address proof
Bank proof such as a cancelled cheque or bank statement
In-person verification record, photograph and signature
Entity documents for non-individual and NRI accounts
outputs: Discrepancy list linked to the relevant documents
Drafted deficiency message to the client
Checklist status by entity type and segment
human_in_the_loop: A checker approves every account, including clean files on the fast track, and resolves each discrepancy. Compliance owns the checklists and acceptable-document rules; the assistant applies them and never overrides a KRA status.
integrations: KRA and CKYC interfaces through your existing integration
guardrails: Aadhaar masked on capture and handled per UIDAI rules
No account approved without a checker
Acceptable-document rules configured and versioned by compliance
Personal data masked in logs and processed in an India region
Every verification result linked to the document and field it came from
compliance_notes: SEBI KYC norms and the KRA framework set what must be collected and verified; the assistant applies your documented checklist and records the maker-checker trail.
Aadhaar is handled per UIDAI rules, and personal data under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: Resident individual accounts and derivatives activation requests from your digital journey, processed in shadow mode next to your checker team.
deliverables: Checklist and rule set agreed with compliance
Working assistant on de-identified historical and live packets
Plan for NRI and non-individual coverage

what_we_measure.how: Assistant outcomes compared with checker decisions on the same packets.
Issues the checker found that the assistant also flagged, and any it missed.
Time per packet with and without the discrepancy list.
Count of client follow-ups needed, compared with a recent baseline period.

faqs.q: Does it handle NRI and corporate accounts?
faqs.a: Yes. Each entity type has its own checklist, for example board resolutions and authorised signatory lists for companies, or overseas address and bank details for NRIs. A typical pilot starts with resident individuals and adds these next.
No. Aadhaar is masked at capture and handled per UIDAI rules. Where DigiLocker or offline e-KYC is used, only the fields your process needs are kept.
No. Clean files move to a fast-track queue, but a checker still approves each one. This keeps the maker-checker control your compliance team relies on.
It checks that a signature is present and legible and can flag obvious differences between the form and other documents. The final signature judgement stays with the checker.
